Synopsis:
An unseasonably intense early spring heatwave struck Australia's east coast, with Brisbane recording its hottest September day since 2019 at 34.4°C. Fire bans were issued across south-east Queensland and greater Sydney, with active bushfires and grass fires reported in multiple locations. Damaging winds compounded conditions, causing jumping castle incidents injuring several children in NSW and Victoria. A cool change was moving up the east coast from Monday, expected to bring relief to both Queensland and NSW. Queensland's winter had been its third-warmest on record, framing the heatwave within a broader pattern of above-average temperatures.
